scientific_question: What molecular pathway can account for formation of the observed trans adamantylated lactone from the specified internal E-alkene acid, and how do the corresponding reaction energetics compare with the specified sulfonamide-tethered E-alkene in TfOH/HFIP?

inputs.content: Carboxylic-acid substrate: (E)-hex-3-enoic acid, HOOC-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-CH3, with E geometry about C3=C4 (carboxyl carbon is C1). SMILES: CC/C=C/CC(=O)O.
Carbon-source reagent: adamantan-1-ol (1-adamantanol), with OH attached at an adamantane bridgehead.

Solvent: hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP), (CF3)2CHOH. Compare reaction energetics in this solvent at 293.15 K. The preparative observations use 0.2 mmol of alkene, 0.2 mmol of 1-adamantanol and TfOH (5 mol%) in HFIP (4.0 mL), at room temperature for 2 h. Room temperature is not assigned an exact numerical value.

The carboxylic-acid substrate forms trans-4-(adamantan-1-yl)-5-ethyloxolan-2-one: the five-membered ring is O-C(=O)-CH2-CH(adamantan-1-yl)-CH(ethyl), closed back to O. The ethyl and adamantan-1-yl substituents are trans; only their relative configuration is specified.

Comparison substrate: N-[(3E)-hex-3-en-1-yl]-4-methylbenzenesulfonamide, p-CH3-C6H4-S(=O)2-NH-CH2-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-CH3, with E alkene geometry. SMILES: CC/C=C/CCNS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1. Its cyclization product is trans-3-(adamantan-1-yl)-2-ethyl-1-(4-methylbenzenesulfonyl)pyrrolidine: the ring is N(SO2-p-C6H4-CH3)-CH(ethyl)-CH(adamantan-1-yl)-CH2-CH2, closed back to N, with trans ethyl/adamantan-1-yl relative configuration.
